“Out of respect for the patient’s privacy, we cannot share any information and we are unable to comment on those involved in patient care,” it said. “Patient safety and exceptional care are our highest priorities.”
Asked how Vincent is doing now, Fiordilino said, “He’s getting better.”
Brewer said that while the boy is home with his family, he has many health challenges.
“Vincent is severely brain-injured,” he said. “He can’t swallow. He seizes up. He can’t sit up on his own or crawl.”

The tragic turn of events began around 5:38 p.m. Feb. 8 with a 911 call for help after Vincent was found floating face down in the family pool and a relative tried to revive him by performing CPR, according to a police report obtained by NBC affiliate KPNX of Phoenix.
Vincent was rushed to the emergency room at Mercy Gilbert Medical Center, where an ER team that included Toosi took over the effort to save him.
At 6:13 p.m., according to the report, Toosi went out to deliver bad news to the boy’s parents.
“As long as there are no objections, I’d like to call time of death,” Toosi said, according to the report.
Then, “at approximately 18:20 hours, Dr. Toosi called the time of death and requested a moment of silence.”
Just as Fiordilino told NBC News, police officers who had been in the ER said in the report that the child still appeared to be gasping for breath after he was declared dead.

A detective reported then hearing “another audible gasp” at around 7:18 p.m. as the ER workers were preparing to move Vincent from the trauma room to the “cold room” that serves as the hospital’s morgue and where the temperature is set at 36 to 39 degrees.
The same detective said that when he returned to photograph the body an hour later, he “again observed what appeared to be a gasp or air release.”
“The nurse again stated it was agonal breathing and explained it was due to compressions, oxygen, and possible pressure applied by family members while saying goodbye,” the report says.
And at 7:23 p.m., “the cold room door was closed,” the report says.
More than four hours later, when the medical examiner’s team arrived at 11:52 p.m. to retrieve the boy, “he was found breathing,” the report says.
“The family was notified immediately,” and the boy was airlifted to Phoenix Children’s Hospital.
Fiordilino said that when she saw her son again in the pediatric intensive care unit, “he was hooked up to all kinds of monitors and things.”
“He looked like a different baby,” she said. “It’s something I hope no other parent has to live through.”

title: Some residents allowed to return home after Toledo chemical release
summary: Dense fog and haze hindered visibility in the Ohio city of about 265,000 people, and residents complained of sore throats and burning eyes.
story: A chemical release at a north Toledo, Ohio, company prompted an evacuation of nearby residents, including some who described concerning health effects and an alarming foglike haze.

Glycol methacrylate, an industrial coating product, was released into the air Tuesday night, Toledo Mayor Wade Kapszukiewicz told reporters Wednesday morning. One person, a first responder, was injured and taken to the hospital, he added, but officials believe the injury is not serious.
Officials do not know what caused the chemical release, which the city clarified was not an explosion.

At 5 p.m. Wednesday, the evacuation zone, which at its peak affected about 1,000 residents within a 1-mile radius, was reduced to a half-mile zone around the facility, and a shelter-in-place order for a 3-mile radius was lifted, the city said.

“Toledo Fire & Rescue hazardous materials personnel are working with federal, state and local partners to monitor conditions, coordinate mitigation efforts, and evaluate next steps,” the city said in an update Wednesday night.

An employee at the company, MC Tank Transport, called 911 to alert authorities to the release Tuesday night, Kapszukiewicz said. He said that the company is headquartered in Arkansas and that executives were on their way to Toledo to assess the situation.
Kapszukiewicz said that when the chemical was released, it became a gas, but when it settles back into the tank, it will turn again into a liquid.
In a statement Wednesday, MC Tank Transport confirmed that “equipment associated with our operations” was involved in the incident and said it was working with emergency authorities.

“We understand the serious disruption this incident has caused to nearby residents and businesses, particularly those required to evacuate their homes,” it said. “We are committed to assisting those affected.”
Haze and irritants
Dense fog and haze hindered visibility in the city of about 265,000 people, and local news stations reported a plasticlike odor.
“That is the chemical whose plume we are monitoring, and we are concerned enough about the health impacts to have taken two actions overnight,” Kapszukiewicz said.
He said people in and around the evacuation zone might react to the chemical in the air — they might taste or smell something unnatural, or their eyes could water. He called that a “real concern.”
But residents should take note of whether those exposures are dangerous or simply annoying.

“There is no question that we’re all kind of smelling and sensing, that there’s something there,” Kapszukiewicz said. “That doesn’t necessarily mean that it is something that is harming us immediately. There are levels of exposure to something like this that are unpleasant but not necessarily dangerous to human health, and that entered into our decision-making in terms of where the shelter-in-place orders took place.”
The chemical is a long-term carcinogen, Toledo Health Commissioner Karim Baroudi said. But he added that there is “no immediate danger” related to Tuesday night’s release.
Baroudi said people who feel irritation from the chemical should shower to wash it off their bodies.

Kapszukiewicz thanked all community agencies that helped respond to the event, including those who assisted in evacuating residents and setting up shelters. He said his administration has been in touch with both the state and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.

“We understand the seriousness of what has happened here,” he said. “That’s why we took the actions that we did. That’s why we’re going to continue to monitor and communicate with the public throughout the day.”
Kapszukiewicz acknowledged the fog hanging over his city Wednesday morning and said that while the chemical release was a factor, the weather also caused natural fog.
For Subscribers

Videos posted to social media and verified by NBC News showed hazy skies as residents in the danger zone drove with their hazard lights on. Streetlamps and car lights were visible through the fog as a line of vehicles appeared to try to leave the area. Some videos appeared to show buses and emergency vehicles in an empty parking lot, surrounded by the fog.
For Subscribers
Another video, taken from a distance, showed thick plumes of smoke gathering in the air. The smoke appeared to be coming from one building.

The tank at MC Tank Terminal is a “transport hub,” said Michael Posadny, the special operations deputy fire chief in charge of hazmat. It keeps products on site briefly before it ships them to their next locations.

Kapszukiewicz said: “In a city like Toledo, with industrial history, events like this, as unpleasant and unwelcome as they are, sometimes happen. And, you know, we have gotten through events like this before. We’ll get through them again.”
‘It’s like a scary movie’

Alicia Cortez was outside walking her dog Tuesday night when she noticed a hazy fog hanging over her area. About 30 minutes later, she told NBC News, she and her husband got alerts on their phones alerting them that hazardous materials were nearby.

When she went back outside, “it was everywhere,” she said. The site was down the street from her family’s home in Toledo. When her husband got through to 911, the dispatcher told him he didn’t have a choice — he had to evacuate immediately.

At around 10:30 p.m., she and her husband packed two cars with their kids, Cortez’s mother-in-law and only the essentials. On their ride to a hotel outside the evacuation zone, “you couldn’t even see in front of you,” she said.

The thick fog was stuck on windshields and cars, Cortez said. It was sticky and burned their eyes. Her mother-in-law got out of the car and walked in front of the group, directing traffic through the haze.

Cortez said her family returned around noon Wednesday to check on their house. She has a headache, and her daughter has a cough. All of their throats are bothering them, she said. The chemical smell was hanging inside their home as her husband taped windows shut to avoid more leaking inside.
They showered the fog off their bodies and retrieved more clothing. They plan to return to the hotel Wednesday night because they “just don’t trust it,” she said.
“It was scary, very scary. It’s like a scary movie,” Cortez said, adding later, “I can’t even believe what I experienced last night.”

Another resident, Emily Downey, told NBC News’ “Top Story” that she awoke on her couch to the smell of chemicals, a bad headache and burning eyes. Her daughter’s eyes were bloodshot, she said, and she had a sore throat.
Downey initially believed her family was far enough from the site that they wouldn’t have to evacuate.
“Then I looked outside, and I was just immediately, like, shocked, because I could barely see anything,” she said. “You can’t see the car across the street.”
Despite the severely limited visibility, she said, her family was able to drive on the expressway and get to her eldest daughter’s home.
“It was probably one of the only times in my life that I really, truly was like, ‘Are we gonna die?’” she said. “That might sound dramatic to some people, but it was very dramatic.”

title: Officer who found man dead in home allegedly assumed his identity
summary: Brian Louis Sguros, 35, responded to the Lauderhill home in July 2022 for a welfare check.
story: Dennis West was found dead in his Florida home during a welfare check in July 2022. Weeks later, one of the officers who discovered his body took possession of the property unlawfully and spent years renovating and impersonating him, according to investigators and police documents.

Brian Louis Sguros, 35, an officer with the Lauderhill Police Department, was arrested Tuesday on felony charges of official misconduct, criminal use of a deceased person’s identification, criminal use of personal identification information, offense against a computer user and unlawful use of a two-way communications device.
It’s not clear whether Sguros has an attorney.
The Broward County Sheriff’s Office said in a news release that Sguros responded to the welfare check at West’s home on July 11, 2022. West, 71, was found dead inside.
The medical examiner determined West died of natural causes from arteriosclerotic cardiovascular disease, according to Sguros’ arrest affidavit.

Sguros presented himself to the medical examiner’s office as West’s friend, though there is no indication that Sguros knew West, according to the sheriff’s office. He also told the office that West had no living family, which was untrue, authorities said.
Sguros stated in paperwork he filed that he took possession of the home in August 2022, weeks after West died, the news release said.

After he took over the home, from August 2022 through February 2025, Sguros cleaned and repaired the property, his arrest affidavit said. Sguros claimed he spent at least $214,000 of his own money on the home.
Sguros also paid taxes and utilities on the home in West’s name, authorities said.

In sworn statements through civil pleadings, Sguros maintained that he took possession of the property and acted because it was hazardous and he wanted to prevent criminal activity and people from squatting, the affidavit said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The investigation found that Sguros had conducted multiple searches within law enforcement databases from his work computer for West’s driver’s license record, the arrest affidavit said. Those searches disclosed West’s address, date of birth, Social Security number and other information, according to the filing.

Sguros is accused of using West’s identification to “get the city of Lauderhill to issue a permit to facilitate repairs,” the release said. He is alleged to have forged West’s signature on the permit application, but the telephone number listed was his own, the arrest affidavit said.

A project manager for a company contracted to replace exterior doors and windows at West’s home in 2024 told police he had no idea West was dead at the time of the work and recalled Sguros’ telling him West was “unavailable.”
In February 2025, Sguros and his spouse filed a form with the Broward County Property Appraiser seeking to establish a claim to the home, according to the affidavit.
The home takeover came to light when a real estate company bought the property from West’s heirs months later, the arrest affidavit said.

The company gained lawful possession of the home in probate proceedings in the fall of 2025, but when one of its employees tried to take possession of it, the employee encountered Sguros, according to the affidavit.

Sguros surrendered the keys to the property before the company’s attorney filed an unlawful detainer action, the affidavit said. But he “demanded reimbursement for repairs and improvements he claimed to have made,” it said.

Sguros filed a complaint against the real estate company in February, saying in filings that he discovered West in the home while he was on duty and detailing how he subsequently began to clean, secure and invest in the property. However, he never established in his records that he came to be involved in the home through a purchase, lease, probate appointment, deed or relationship with West’s heirs, the arrest affidavit said.
In the civil litigation, Sguros sought more than $200,000 for the work he said he performed on the home, the affidavit said.
In May, an attorney for the company submitted a complaint to the Lauderhill Police Department.
Sguros appeared in court Wednesday and was ordered held on a $25,000 bond, NBC South Florida reported. After his arrest, he was placed on administrative leave without pay from the police department.

title: Rep. Ilhan Omar details federal search of her D.C. home, says she’ll have to move for safety
summary: The Minnesota Democrat said her husband and son were home when federal agents began banging on her house doors at 6 a.m. before they conducted an hourslong search.
story: Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., on Wednesday described in detail for the first time the early-morning search of her home last week by federal agents, revealing in the process that she can no longer live there because of safety concerns.

In an interview with MS NOW, Omar said she and her husband were initially startled and confused by the arrival of agents with Homeland Security Investigations, who began banging on their doors and yelling at 6 a.m. Oct. 12.
“Well, I mean, you don’t show up to somebody’s house that early in the morning unless you were trying to freak them out, and, you know, it obviously did freak all of us out,” Omar said.

Federal agents searched Omar’s home as part of a criminal investigation that has alarmed Justice Department veterans who cited its proximity to the midterm elections. A person familiar with the investigation has told NBC News that the possible charges against Omar include conspiracy and making false statements in immigration paperwork.
Omar told MS NOW she had “only had 2½ hours of sleep” when the agents arrived since she had returned home from a trip in the early morning.

“It was, you know, trying to figure out, like you’re dreaming, this weird thing that’s happening,” Omar said. “But they basically, like, surrounded the house. They were pounding, pounding on the back door and the front door.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

She said she and her husband yelled down to try to communicate that they were coming downstairs momentarily as they rushed to get dressed. Omar added that one of her three children, her 20-year-old son, was also at the residence.

“I thought something was on fire. I thought something was happening to the neighbor,” Omar said, adding that she was particularly confused when she saw HSI agents at the door, since they often focus on issues like human trafficking, drugs, cybersecurity and terrorism.
“The fact that they were at my house that early in the morning, you know, was so, so bizarre,” she said. “I was like, ‘Why are you here?’”

Omar said the agents presented her with a warrant at the door after she asked to see one. They then asked her to sign a paper that would waive certain rights she has as a member of Congress, Omar said, adding that she declined to sign it.
Under the Speech or Debate Clause of the Constitution, members of Congress are protected from civil and criminal liability relating to their legislative acts.

Omar said in the interview that the agents took 17 items from her home, including old phones belonging to her and one of her daughters. Seizing the phone of a sitting member of Congress typically triggers a set of law enforcement protocols to ensure the Speech or Debate Clause is upheld.
The search took “four or five hours,” Omar told MS NOW.

“I don’t think I was able to call my attorney until about an hour into the search,” she said. Asked what she was doing during that time, she said, “I sat on the couch, staring at the warrant, trying to make sure that they were staying within the bounds of what the warrant allowed them to do.”
The Department of Homeland Security referred NBC News to the Justice Department, which did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Omar’s account of the search.

In addition to the phones, Omar said, agents took multiple items belonging to her husband, Tim Mynett, including a camera that was passed down by his uncle, a Somali phrase book that he was using to learn the language and his notebooks.
Omar said that according to the receipt she was given after the search, she does not believe the agents took anything with her DNA. She also said she was not asked to provide a DNA sample.
Overall, Omar said, the agents “mostly conducted themselves in a decent way.”
“They did a really good job in putting everything back in its place,” Omar said. “They actually even folded some of my clothing that were not folded.”
Still, Omar criticized the federal investigation.

“The people who knocked on my door, searching for papers, literally have his papers,” Omar said, referring to the paperwork filed by her late father. “They are the ones who processed us to come to the United States.”
She said that after the search, she can no longer live at her Washington home.

“Obviously, I can’t continue to live there, because our address has been public,” Omar said. “And with the death threats that I deal with, it’s not, it’s no longer going to be feasible to be in that house and have my kids, like, visiting off and on having people track them.”
Omar rejected President Donald Trump’s insistence that he had “nothing to do” with the investigation.
“I mean, he’s got everything to do with it,” she said. “You know, this goes back to 2019 when he was screaming about the fact that, you know, I, I need to be sent back, I need to be deported.”
Omar has been a frequent target of Trump since his first term. He has called her “garbage,” accused her of fraud and called for her deportation.
Omar said she feels “confident in my truth” as she again denied the allegations against her.

“How more obvious could these people be? You know, it’s, like, you could at least have the appearance of not having this be fictitious,” Omar said. “But they’ve chosen to blatantly have every character that has been involved be someone who has expressed explicitly that they don’t want me to be in the United States.”

title: Vance says Republicans should ‘stop whining’ about Vivek Ramaswamy’s attack ad
summary: Vice President JD Vance told Republicans to “stop whining” about Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy’s controversial ad featuring his Democratic opponent Amy Acton’s estranged mother.
story: Vice President JD Vance told Republicans to “stop whining” about Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy’s controversial ad featuring his Democratic opponent Amy Acton’s estranged mother.

“Politics is a tough business, and my message to my fellow elected Republicans is if you actually believe in the things you say you believe in, stop whining about an advertisement and go win the race in 13 days,” Vance told reporters Wednesday in Cincinnati.
Ramaswamy’s ad targeting Acton exploded across the political landscape Tuesday, sparking criticism from both sides of the aisle in the final stretch of the battleground governor’s race.
Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, who is running for a full term after he was appointed to fill Vance’s former seat, said he “would not have run that ad.”

Ramaswamy’s ad features Acton’s estranged mother calling her a “liar” and urging Ohioans not to vote for her. Acton previously recounted being sexually abused by her mother’s husband as a child, and Acton’s brother said Tuesday that their “birth mother stayed married to Amy’s rapist until he died.”
Acton said in a 2019 interview with The Youngstown Vindicator that she had not seen her mother since a hearing in the 1978 court case against her stepfather.

Conservative commentator Meghan McCain said on X that the ad was “dastardly” and “never should have been created.” An aide for Sen. Mike Lee, R-Utah, deleted his post that shared the video. The aide, Dan Hauser, apologized and said he deleted his post “after researching it, and the disturbing allegations.”
Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., called it “the most shameful, disgusting, offensive ad this election season.”

Mace, an advocate for women and girls who have faced assault, told CNN that she had been “a real big Vivek Ramaswamy fan” but that “this was just deeply offensive, and I just can’t believe this is what passes for decency in this election.”

Vance brushed off concerns about the ad, instead criticizing Republicans who condemned it. Speaking to reporters in Ohio on Wednesday, he said that “whether the ad was appropriate or not is not really my concern,” adding that he was focused on who would win the elections.
Vance says GOP should 'stop whining' about Ramaswamy ad

“I have to admit that I’m a little bit disgusted when I see Republicans across the country who are whining more about that advertisement than they are about what the congressional Democrats and other Democrats want to do to the United States of America,” he said.
He also urged Republicans to “remember some of the ads that have been run against me” and other Republicans.
Vance brought up the ad at an Ohio rally Wednesday afternoon. He said he “wasn’t even supposed to talk about” the controversy, “but I cannot help myself.”

“Now, the media and the Democrats of the state of Ohio are obsessed, because guess what, Vivek Ramaswamy had the audacity to run a TV commercial which calls it out like it is and calls Amy Acton a liar.”
“My message, ladies and gentlemen, is very simple: Whatever you think about any of the TV advertisements, focus on the substance and focus on the facts,” he said, going on to criticize Acton.
Vance’s and Ramaswamy’s political circles have notable overlaps. NBC News has reported that several members of Ramaswamy’s campaign previously worked on Vance’s political team.
Ramaswamy’s team plans a $4 million statewide advertising push around the ad.
Acton’s brother, Philip Stearns, responded to the ad Tuesday, slamming Ramaswamy.

“It’s not surprising that Vivek Ramaswamy has stooped to such a despicable low as to attempt to turn the sexual abuse Amy endured at 12 years old from our birth mother’s husband into a political talking point,” Stearns said.
Stearns said he and his sister were removed from their mother and stepfather’s custody after their stepfather was arrested.
Attempts to reach Acton’s mother, Donna Arthur, by phone and email Tuesday were unsuccessful.

title: Supreme Court rejects Trump policy restricting treatment for transgender inmates
summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday said the Trump administration cannot enforce a new policy that restricts treatment for transgender inmates in federal prison.
story: WASHINGTON — In a blow to President Donald Trump, the Supreme Court said Wednesday that his administration cannot enforce a new policy that restricts treatment for transgender inmates in federal prison.

The justices in a brief order rejected an emergency application filed by the administration that sought to block a lower court injunction against the proposal. The court order included no explanation, saying only that two conservative justices, Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito, would have granted it.
There are about 1,000 transgender inmates in federal custody.

“This is a critical ruling for our clients and all transgender people in Bureau of Prisons custody,” Li Nowlin-Sohl, a lawyer with the American Civil Liberties Union representing the plaintiffs, said in a statement.
“The denial of medically necessary health care, including gender-affirming health care, to people in prison is a violation of their fundamental constitutional rights,” she added.

The policy, which will continue to be litigated over in lower courts, is part of President Donald Trump’s broader effort to roll back moves to expand transgender rights. It was announced in line with his January 2025 executive order telling federal agencies not to acknowledge the concept of gender identity outside of the “immutable biological classification” of male or female.

“This order is a loss for common sense,” White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster said in a statement. The administration will continue its efforts to “protect countless Americans from these dangerous, life-altering medical practices,” she added.

In several different announcements, the Bureau of Prisons over the last 18 months has said it will not provide gender transition surgery, hormone treatments or “social accommodations” such as wigs, padding or makeup.

That rolled back previous policies that allowed for gender-affirming care, with the government saying that such treatments have recently been called into question by medical professionals. That claim is heavily contested by transgender rights advocates.
If the policy had gone into effect, the only treatment transgender inmates would have been able to receive would be mental health services and potentially medications like antidepressants.

A group of transgender inmates sued, arguing the government had failed to adequately explain the change. They also alleged a violation of the Constitution’s Eighth Amendment, which bars cruel and unusual punishment.
The lead plaintiffs in the case, Alishea Kingdom, Jas Kapule and Solo Nichols, have all been receiving hormone treatment for several years.
For Subscribers

Washington-based U.S. District Judge Royce Lamberth blocked the current policy in a ruling earlier this year, concluding that the Bureau of Prisons had failed to consider the merits of its past treatment of transgender inmates in formulating the plan.
For Subscribers

“Despite providing gender-affirming care to inmates in its custody for years, the government cites in the Program Statement zero evidence from its own medical or mental health professionals to support its conclusions,” he wrote. The government provided no evidence that the previous plan was “ineffective or harmful,” he added.
Lamberth, a Reagan appointee, also found that the proposal appeared to be engineered precisely to comply with the president’s executive order, concluding that the reasons given were pretextual.
In September, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit rejected a Trump administration request seeking to block the judge’s final decision, with the panel split 2-1.

In court papers, Solicitor General D. John Sauer said the lower court was guilty of “substituting its own policy judgment for that of the agency” and was essentially faulting the Bureau of Prisons for following the president’s executive order.
ACLU lawyers said in court papers that the Bureau of Prisons has provided hormone therapy to inmates since 1992 while also gradually expanding access to other treatments and social accommodations.

The abrupt change without necessary explanation “gives rise to the inference that the agency’s purported reasons were not its actual reasons,” the lawyers wrote. “That glaring omission, as well as the unreasonableness of its decision, make it clear that the rationales were contrived to support the demand President Trump made” in the executive order.
The case marks a rare recent win for transgender advocates at the Supreme Court, which has a 6-3 conservative majority.

In June, the court upheld state bans on transgender athletes seeking to participate in women’s and girls’ sports. A year earlier, the court backed state laws banning gender transition treatments for transgender youths.
The court has also allowed Trump to implement a ban on transgender people in the military.

title: The NBA star helping protect his opponents’ feet
summary: NBA star Damian Lillard co-founded an insoles company. It turns out his biggest competition on the court is wearing them.
story: Before they even stepped out onto an NBA court as teammates, Portland Trail Blazers point guard Damian Lillard dished out an assist to his backcourt mate Ja Morant.
At the start of the team’s preseason training camp, Morant was getting ready to put on his shoes when he mentioned to Lillard that he needed more pairs of the orthotics he was using.
“You know that’s my company, right?” Lillard told Morant, who initially thought he was joking.

Lillard hasn’t gone around the NBA evangelizing his product, but as Morant’s usage showed, it turns out he hasn’t needed to. Move Insoles, the company Lillard co-founded with longtime athlete marketer Nate Jones, has already been widely adopted by athletes across multiple sports.

Jones, who works at Goodwin Sports, the agency that represents Lillard, began working on Move in earnest in 2019. He courted Lillard as a co-founder and other NBA stars, such as Chris Paul and Jamal Crawford, as investors. Jones estimates that 25 NBA teams now use the product, in addition to non-NBA stars such as the Dallas Cowboys’ CeeDee Lamb and five-time WNBA MVP A’Ja Wilson.
And like Morant, those teams and players are using the insoles not because of a corporate partnership or at Lillard’s request but because of word of mouth.

“I’ve been watching the NBA and been an NBA junkie my entire life,” Jones said. “So to create something that these players rely on, believe in, that their medical staffs rely on and believe in, is a big deal.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Lillard was eager to be an active participant in the company because of his own experiences. He has been using orthotics in his shoes to help recover from a broken foot he sustained at Weber State. Early in his NBA career, Lillard also dealt with plantar fasciitis, but he couldn’t find the right insole that was both comfortable and not a hindrance to his performance.

“Needing more support in my shoe, especially having flat feet and the amount of miles on my feet, I understood the importance of not only having support in your shoe, but the right type of support and different options for different people,” Lillard said.

He hasn’t simply slapped his name on Move; he has also made himself an integral part of the product development. Lillard has personally tested each of the four insoles Move sells, which range from a more comfort-oriented orthotic to more performance-oriented ones.
Practicing with Team USA ahead of the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, Lillard was testing prototypes and giving feedback to Jones.

“Me being somebody that’s going to be on the floor, somebody that’s had these [foot] issues that I mentioned and also having real friendships with the people that I’m partnering with, they know I’m gonna tell the truth,” Lillard said.

Jones said the biggest advantage of working with Lillard was his honesty, saying Lillard “won’t sugarcoat it” when it comes to his opinions. Now, not only is it common for Lillard to see other players wearing his signature shoe on the court; after games he’ll see players pulling out the insole he tested years earlier.
Over the last year, as he missed all of the 2025-26 season with a torn Achilles, Lillard had extra time to devote to his business interests.

“At this stage of my career and having that much time, I’m thinking about ‘What do I see for my kids, and how do I want to try to help them more? What about when I’m not playing? What do I want to spend my time doing?’” he said.

He added that working on Move reaffirmed his interest in business opportunities that allow him to be involved from the ground up. Lillard and Jones still have further goals for their insoles, including targeting the youth sports market so athletes are aware of their foot health at younger ages.

Move is also announcing soon that it will be an official partner of the National Basketball Athletic Trainers Association, which means it’s even likelier that some of Lillard’s opponents will have him to thank for helping their feet.

Just don’t expect Lillard to aggressively pitch the product now that he’s ready to resume his NBA career. He laughed when he was asked whether he’s considered trying to find an investment on the TV show “Shark Tank.”

“I’ve watched the show, and I’ve had thoughts,” he acknowledged. “It would be a hard show for me personally to be on, just because I would want to be prepared 1,000%. I wouldn’t want to have the responsibility of still being an active player.”
For now, that means Lillard will have to settle for advertising by what he does on the court.

title: Tennessee Titans cut DL Jordan Elliott, saying he took a gun to team facility
summary: The seventh-year pro had played in Tennessee’s first five games this season before he was sidelined Sunday.
story: The Tennessee Titans cut defensive lineman Jordan Elliott after he took a gun to the team’s training facility in a “terrible lapse of judgment,” officials said Wednesday.
Titans coach Robert Saleh defended Elliott and called him “a good man” who deserves another chance — just not in Tennessee.
“He’s a good man [who] had a terrible lapse in judgment that I recognize as a call for help more than a criminal act,” Saleh told reporters. “It’s unfortunate the way it went down.”
Union officials and Elliott’s agent could not immediately be reached for comment Wednesday.
It wasn’t immediately clear what might have prompted Elliott to take a firearm to the team’s Nashville headquarters.
Nashville police were not called and did not respond to the scene, the police department said Wednesday.

“The league’s firearm policy prohibits any personnel from bringing a firearm to club facilities, stadiums, and team hotels and on team planes or buses,” the NFL said in a statement Wednesday. “The club promptly notified the league of the matter which is under review.”
For Subscribers
Elliott had played in Tennessee’s first five games this season before he was listed as inactive Sunday for “not injury related, personal” reasons.
Then, by Tuesday, he was off the team.
“On Thursday, October 15, there was an incident at our team facility involving Jordan Elliott,” the Titans said in a statement.
For Subscribers
“Following our review of the incident, we have made the decision to release Elliott from our roster. We will have no further comment on the matter.”
Elliott signed with Tennessee in the offseason, following two years with the San Francisco 49ers and four previous campaigns with the Cleveland Browns.
Elliott’s move to Nashville made for a reunion with Titans first-year coach Saleh, who was the 49ers’ defensive coordinator last season.
Saleh said that he hopes Elliott can sign with another team and that he’d vouch for his character.
“Unfortunately, rules are rules with regards to guns on [team] property,” Saleh said.
“My message to 31 other teams would be: If you need a hell of a run-stopping D tackle that can help you on a playoff run, give me a call. I’ll tell you everything you need to know about him.”
Elliott, 28, a Houston native, played college football for the Texas Longhorns and the Missouri Tigers before he was taken by Cleveland in the third round of the 2020 NFL draft.
“At the end of the day, we’re all humans,” quarterback Cam Ward said. “We’re all with him. I mean, he’s a great person.”

title: Officer who found man dead in home allegedly assumed his identity
summary: Brian Louis Sguros, 35, responded to the Lauderhill home in July 2022 for a welfare check.
story: Dennis West was found dead in his Florida home during a welfare check in July 2022. Weeks later, one of the officers who discovered his body took possession of the property unlawfully and spent years renovating and impersonating him, according to investigators and police documents.

Brian Louis Sguros, 35, an officer with the Lauderhill Police Department, was arrested Tuesday on felony charges of official misconduct, criminal use of a deceased person’s identification, criminal use of personal identification information, offense against a computer user and unlawful use of a two-way communications device.
It’s not clear whether Sguros has an attorney.
The Broward County Sheriff’s Office said in a news release that Sguros responded to the welfare check at West’s home on July 11, 2022. West, 71, was found dead inside.
The medical examiner determined West died of natural causes from arteriosclerotic cardiovascular disease, according to Sguros’ arrest affidavit.

Sguros presented himself to the medical examiner’s office as West’s friend, though there is no indication that Sguros knew West, according to the sheriff’s office. He also told the office that West had no living family, which was untrue, authorities said.
Sguros stated in paperwork he filed that he took possession of the home in August 2022, weeks after West died, the news release said.

After he took over the home, from August 2022 through February 2025, Sguros cleaned and repaired the property, his arrest affidavit said. Sguros claimed he spent at least $214,000 of his own money on the home.
Sguros also paid taxes and utilities on the home in West’s name, authorities said.

In sworn statements through civil pleadings, Sguros maintained that he took possession of the property and acted because it was hazardous and he wanted to prevent criminal activity and people from squatting, the affidavit said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The investigation found that Sguros had conducted multiple searches within law enforcement databases from his work computer for West’s driver’s license record, the arrest affidavit said. Those searches disclosed West’s address, date of birth, Social Security number and other information, according to the filing.

Sguros is accused of using West’s identification to “get the city of Lauderhill to issue a permit to facilitate repairs,” the release said. He is alleged to have forged West’s signature on the permit application, but the telephone number listed was his own, the arrest affidavit said.

A project manager for a company contracted to replace exterior doors and windows at West’s home in 2024 told police he had no idea West was dead at the time of the work and recalled Sguros’ telling him West was “unavailable.”
In February 2025, Sguros and his spouse filed a form with the Broward County Property Appraiser seeking to establish a claim to the home, according to the affidavit.
The home takeover came to light when a real estate company bought the property from West’s heirs months later, the arrest affidavit said.

The company gained lawful possession of the home in probate proceedings in the fall of 2025, but when one of its employees tried to take possession of it, the employee encountered Sguros, according to the affidavit.

Sguros surrendered the keys to the property before the company’s attorney filed an unlawful detainer action, the affidavit said. But he “demanded reimbursement for repairs and improvements he claimed to have made,” it said.

Sguros filed a complaint against the real estate company in February, saying in filings that he discovered West in the home while he was on duty and detailing how he subsequently began to clean, secure and invest in the property. However, he never established in his records that he came to be involved in the home through a purchase, lease, probate appointment, deed or relationship with West’s heirs, the arrest affidavit said.
In the civil litigation, Sguros sought more than $200,000 for the work he said he performed on the home, the affidavit said.
In May, an attorney for the company submitted a complaint to the Lauderhill Police Department.
Sguros appeared in court Wednesday and was ordered held on a $25,000 bond, NBC South Florida reported. After his arrest, he was placed on administrative leave without pay from the police department.

title: ‘Love Is Blind’ Stars Stew and Jax Reveal Where They Stand After Awkward Breakup
summary: “Love Is Blind” Season 11 stars Jax and Stew tell TODAY.com how their relationship has unfolded since the show ended.
story: Warning: Spoilers from “Love Is Blind” Season 11 below…
After her ghosting moment that went viral, Jacqueline “Jax” Guelli decided to reunite with ex-fiancé Scott “Stew” Stewart in the newest episodes of “Love Is Blind” to explain her hasty departure.
So far, the most talked about moment of Season 11 of the Netflix reality dating show has been Jax’s reaction after meeting Stew for the first time.

Following their engagement in the pods, Jax and Stew saw each other face-to-face, and the feelings were no longer mutual. She informed the producers that she wanted to leave the show immediately and return home, without breaking up with Stew in person. Producers told him about her abrupt exit, and shared the news that Jax didn’t want to leave any contact information for Stew.

But in Episode 6, the two had a sit-down in Boston to unpack their broken engagement. Stew asked why Jax didn’t want to have a conversation before leaving. She said she should have spoken to him and he didn’t deserve how she treated him. She also shared that her family and friends encouraged her to chat with him.
Jax then told Stew she expected to be “blown away” by their connection in real life, but she wasn’t.
In response, Stew asked, “Is that our cue to leave?” They had another confusing exit and didn’t appear again in the second batch of episodes.
Stew reveals the status of their relationship in an interview with TODAY.com.

“I think the pods was such an intense experience, and it accelerates relationships so much that I think we both kind of lost our bearing once we got back to the real world,” he says. “I think it just took some time for each of us to resettle, reconnect with our friends and family (and) reconnect with normal life.”
As for where the two currently stand, he says, “Since then we’ve been great friends, and the relationship has continued.”
In a separate interview, Jax clarifies to TODAY.com that it wasn’t the opinions of her friends and family that pushed her to meet Stew on camera.
“We definitely needed to talk. And I was happy and I was excited to see him,” she says.
The two will likely reveal more about how they mended their relationship at the upcoming Season 11 reunion. The date of the reunion has yet to be announced.

title: Craig Melvin Wins His People’s Sexiest Man Alive Poll ... and Gets Crowned on TODAY!
summary: Craig Melvin has won the “hotter than your cup of coffee in the morning” category in the People’s Sexiest Man Alive Readers’ Choice poll.
story: Craig Melvin is hot!
The TODAY co-anchor has won the “hotter than your cup of coffee in the morning” category in the People’s Sexiest Man Alive Readers’ Choice poll.
Craig beat out Michael Strahan, Gio Benitez and Vladimir Duthiers for the title, with readers voting on the question: “Which of these morning hosts is hotter than your first cup of coffee?”

“We we are happy to announce, ladies and gentlemen, that our friend Craig here is officially hotter than a cup of coffee this morning,” Carson Daly announced on the Oct. 22 episode of TODAY. “You have been voted People magazine’s sexiest morning show host.”
Craig was recognized for his feat with a towel with the “sexiest man alive” logo on it, along with a crown and a sash.
“Come on, you’re the king,” Al Roker said.
“Long may you reign,” Savannah Guthrie said.
Carson made a joke that Craig got the towel because the magazine knows he sweats a lot.
“Now we know why he sweats. It’s because he’s so hot,” Savannah said.
Craig, who was playfully egged on to give a speech, took the award in stride.
“Glad it’s over,” he said.
“Thanks to my mom and my wife who voted at least 100, 200 times, for sure,” he added.
His wife, Lindsay Czarniak, was also thrilled with the honor.
“He’s just sexy in everything she does,” she said when she appeared from home on the 3rd hour of TODAY on Oct. 22.
“This doesn’t mean that you have to stop doing things, but it’s sort of like you know everything can get a little sexier, like sexy cooking, right?” she joked.
After some jokes about Craig doing chores around the house while shirtless, Lindsay then turned a little bit more serious.

“One of the things I thought of first was my grandma, she’s going to be so excited because she lives for watching you and this show,” she said. “And I tried to call her this morning because I was like, ‘You’re just not going to believe it.’ And this is really cool.”
She ended with a message for her husband. “I do think you’re sexy, but I am really proud of you because you know you’re sexy at heart, as well,” she said.
Craig was nominated for the honor last month and took it in stride. His co-anchors became some of his biggest cheerleaders, with Savannah Guthrie encouraging viewers to “vote early and often.”
“Am I being punk’d right now?” Craig said on TODAY Sept. 30 of his nomination.
Lindsay also made sure to campaign for him. Craig and Lindsay, who have been married since 2011, share two children, Delano, 12, and Sybil, 9.

“He is an amazing dad, tremendous husband, teammate, partner, always so supportive and encouraging,” she said in an Instagram reel posted Oct. 12. “He makes a mean chili ... he is a pro at candle-making. He is really good at debating. This is true — and I mean in the most positive of ways.
“But beyond that, he is someone who really cares about where he’s from, leaves people feeling really good about themselves in his presence,” she continued.

“And beyond all those things that make him sexy on the outside — like, let’s be honest, the dimple, guys, it’s the dimple — I think it’s his character and his makeup on the inside that make us think that really, you know, he’s the sexiest man alive.”
Craig had previously appeared in People’s Readers’ Choice poll. In 2023, he was nominated for sexiest morning show host, but lost out to Mark Consuelos.

title: How to Read All of Sarah J. Maas’ Books In Order
summary: So you’re considering jumping down the rabbit hole that is author Sarah J. Maas’ sprawling catalog of romantasy books.
story: So you’re considering jumping down the rabbit hole that is author Sarah J. Maas’ sprawling catalog of romantasy books. You’ve heard about her, perhaps through BookTok or your reading buddies or her legions of fans who can’t get enough. You know about her three series — “Throne of Glass,” “A Court of Thorns and Roses” and “Crescent City”— and her forthcoming books, “A Court of Splintered Harmony” and “A Court of Forgotten Melody,” have only heightened your interest.
So you want to join in on the fun. But where do you begin? And what order should you be reading?
If you’re overwhelmed — 18 books might do that — fret not. We’ll help you get started.
More on Sarah J. Maas and ‘ACOTAR’
Sarah J. Maas Is BookTok’s Reigning Romantasy Queen. All Rise‘A Court of Thorns and Roses’ Books 6 and 7 Titles and Covers Revealed by Sarah J. Maas
Sarah J. Maas Is BookTok’s Reigning Romantasy Queen. All Rise
‘A Court of Thorns and Roses’ Books 6 and 7 Titles and Covers Revealed by Sarah J. Maas
Sarah J. Maas Books to Read First
There are two key things to note when getting started:
It doesn’t matter if you read the “Throne of Glass” books or the “ACOTAR” books first.
Read the “ACOTAR” books before you pick up the “Crescent City” books.

If you’re debating whether to start with “Throne of Glass” or “ACOTAR,” it depends on your preference: “ACOTAR” is romance forward — if you lean toward that genre, start there. “Throne of Glass” is big on the epic fantasy elements — you lean toward that, start there.
‘Throne of Glass’ Series Reading Order

“Throne of Glass” is Maas’ first book she published in 2012, and it eventually became a series of eight books in total. Maas on her website lists her preferred reading order, which is the publication order. It looks as such:
“Throne of Glass” (2012)
“Crown of Midnight” (2013)
“The Assassin’s Blade” (2014)
“Heir of Fire” (2014)
“Queen of Shadows” (2015)
“Empire of Storms” (2016)
“Tower of Dawn” (2017)
“Kingdom of Ash” (2018)

“The Assassin’s Blade” is a prequel (technically a collection of novellas) that Maas published after the first two books were released and features characters that crop up later the book series. Because of that, some argue that reading the series in the story’s chronological order is beneficial. If you choose to do that, Maas and her publishers at Bloomsbury have said that’s fine too — it doesn’t spoil anything.

There’s a community of fans who created a way for people to read “Empire of Storms” and “Tower of Dawn” at the same time, by switching back and forth between chunks of chapters. These two penultimate books take place in two different locations but at the same point in the story. For those interested in the tandem read, here is a PDF that you can refer to.
‘ACOTAR’ Series Reading Order

“A Court of Thorns and Roses,” also known by its acronym “ACOTAR,” is typically the gateway into the SJM universe. The highly anticipated sixth and seven books in the series were announced in August and will be released Oct. 28, 2026, and Jan. 12, 2027, respectively.
The “ACOTAR” series should be read in publishing order, which is also the story’s chronological order:
“A Court of Thorns and Roses” (2015)
“A Court of Mist and Fury” (2016)
“A Court of Wings and Ruin” (2017)
“A Court of Frost and Starlight” (2018)
“A Court of Silver Flames” (2021)
“A Court of Splintered Harmony” (Oct. 28, 2026)
“A Court of Forgotten Melody” (Jan. 12, 2027)
‘Crescent City’ Series Reading Order

The “Crescent City” series contains three novels (though Maas told TODAY in 2023 that a fourth is on the horizon). As Maas and her publishers at Bloomsbury have noted, “you may find the ‘Crescent City’ reading experience more rewarding if you pick up the ‘Court of Thorns and Roses’ series first.”
Like “ACOTAR,” the recommended reading order for “Crescent City” is the publishing order:
“House of Earth and Blood” (2020)
“House of Sky and Breath” (2022)
“House of Flame and Shadow” (2024)

title: Our 1 Big Question for Jackie Tohn During Commercial: Are Sasha and Esther End Game in ‘Nobody Wants This’?
summary: Jackie Tohn talks about whether Sasha and Esther will end up together in Season 3 of “Nobody Wants This” and what she makes of Morgan and Sasha.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on air.
Warning: This story contains spoilers for Season 3 of “Nobody Wants This.”
Esther breaks free from her marriage in the third season of “Nobody Wants This.” But does she like what’s on the other side?
Jackie Tohn, in an interview with TODAY.com, says she’s just like viewers in that she comes to new seasons excited to find out what happens to her character.

“People always ask me, ‘What do you want to happen?’ And I’m like, ‘I’m like you guys. I’m like the fans. I want to see what the showrunners and writers come up with. It’s not for me to say what happens.’ It’s really exciting,” she says.
In the third season, Esther moves forward with her separation from Sasha (Timothy Simons). Living alone for the first time, she gets a real estate degree and finds connections via online dating.

Meanwhile, Sasha explores that long-simmering tension between him and Morgan (Justine Lupe), the sister of his brother’s fiancée. After that, Sasha and Esther have one night together that makes it all the more complicated.

It comes to a head in the finale, when Esther learns about Morgan and Sasha (and so does Sasha’s mom), making Joanne (Kristen Bell) and Noah (Adam Brody) seem like the most stable couple in the group.
Below, we unpack that love triangle and the plot twists that ensue.

In Season 2, Esther sort of threatened to be a good time. She wasn’t yet, but she was like, “I’m fun too. Why is everyone else fun? I’m fun.” And in Season 3, she’s really putting her money where her mouth is and being like, “What does my life look like outside of being a wife and a mother?”

She gets a job for the first time since she’s had a kid. She gets her real estate license. She goes on the apps. She tries to figure out, if she had asked herself all of these big life questions, (where) would she be? Would this be where she’d be? What would she want to do? Who would she want to be with? And maybe it is Sasha. It’s a huge, huge season of self-discovery, growth for her.
It’s a huge growth season for him. I think for Noah and Joanne, it’s very “champagney” and delicious.

Meanwhile, Sasha’s sort of forced to face the music. Then he makes the first mature decision of his life, where he’s in this situation with Morgan and he’s like, “I don’t know what this is, or if this is anything, but certainly right now is not the time.” And so he’s making all these mature decisions, which I think before he maybe didn’t have the balls to do.
Completely different. From Morgan he gets (something) fun, wild.

With Esther, there’s obviously love there. There’s history. There’s stability. They have a daughter, and I do think Sasha and Esther love each other. Because he was a little bit gentler, he needed a fire lit under his ass, and that fire was Esther. I think a lot of people need that kind of partner that’s going to push them to be better, and Esther does all of that for him.
Morgan has always been this fun friend, but now maybe there is something more there. There is a depth there where they both are the sort of the “loser” sibling, but they see something in each other.
I think I have skin in the game. But in my brain, I think it’s Esther. I really do. I must think that because I’m her. I just feel like in my heart, Sasha and Esther go together.

Bina for sure. Esther can be as upset as she wants, but she made her bed, right? She literally said to him, “I am going to go do this. You should too.” So he did. And yeah, she’s hurt. But Bina’s like, “Great, now this son is ruining the family.”

I think that it’s sort of happening in that she’s always been so serious, and I’m so goofy. I like that in Season 3, she’s a little bit more like, “Oh my God, I’m nervous. What do I do? Where do I go?” She doesn’t have it as together as she does in Season 1 and Season 2. She’s just the boss and she knows where everything is. She knows how to be and what to do. And in Season 3, she’s a little bit more fumbling. I think it’s sweet to show her vulnerability in that way.

title: Who Is Koschei the Deathless? What to Remember About the Next ‘ACOTAR’ Villain
summary: When author Sarah J. Maas announced the next two installments of her “A Court of Thorns and Roses” series this summer, both books’ synopses named only one specific character: Koschei the Deathless.
story: When author Sarah J. Maas announced the next two installments of her “A Court of Thorns and Roses” series this summer, both books’ synopses named only one specific character: Koschei the Deathless.

If you’re among those who reacted with an echoing “who?”, that’s understandable. The last book in the series, “A Court of Silver Flames,” had us focused on Blood Rites and Valkyries and all that Nesta-Cassian romancing. The looming threat facing the world? Consider it reader amnesia.

The gist: While the prior books had Feyre, Rhysand and the Night Court gang battling and defeating Hybern, an island west of Prythian whose king wanted to reclaim the Fae’s dominance, the team is now pivoting to a new big bad who’s way more dangerous.
For those in need of a quick Koschei refresher, we’ve got you. Here’s a summary before heading into “ACOTAR” Book 6, “A Court of Splintered Harmony.”
Read More on “ACOTAR”

Sarah J. Maas Is BookTok’s Reigning Romantasy Queen. All RiseHow to Read ‘ACOTAR’ Author Sarah J. Maas’ Books in OrderInside ‘A Court of Thorns and Roses’ and the Sprawling Romantasy Universe That Has TikTok Obsessed
Sarah J. Maas Is BookTok’s Reigning Romantasy Queen. All Rise
How to Read ‘ACOTAR’ Author Sarah J. Maas’ Books in Order
Inside ‘A Court of Thorns and Roses’ and the Sprawling Romantasy Universe That Has TikTok Obsessed
Koschei is a ‘Death-God’ and Sibling to the Bone Carver and Weaver
Let’s start by going back a few books to the third in the series, “A Court of Wings and Ruin,” in which Koschei receives his first mention.

In Chapters 22 and 23, Cassian and Feyre are visiting the Prison, a place beneath a mountain where dangerous beings are locked away, to recruit an insidious creature called the Bone Carver to fight alongside Prythian in the war against Hybern. They are prepared to offer the Carver a way back to the world from which he originated, but the Carver insists his home is long gone and wishes to stay within the safety of his prison cell.

He’s hiding, he says, from his two powerful siblings: his twin sister, Stryga, also known as the Weaver of the Wood, and their older brother, Koschei. Both “fell” into this world with him long before Prythian existed. Together they are “death-gods,” meaning they feed on life itself, but he says his brother and sister are more powerful than he.
Koschei is Confined to a Far Away Lake
During that conversation at the Prison, the Carver tells Feyre and Cassian that Stryga and Koschei were worshipped and feared by the ancient Fae before they were captured by a “clever” Fae warrior.
“She could not kill them in the end — they were too strong. They could only be contained,” the Carver says. “I knew that long before she ever trapped them — took it upon myself to find my way here.”
His siblings have been imprisoned since: Stryga is confined to a cottage in Prythian’s unmapped area called the Middle. Koschei is bound to a lake on the continent east of Prythian.
Hybern, with the Cauldron’s possession, ends up taking out the Bone Carver and Stryga in the war. Koschei, meanwhile, is still at his lake, but he’s been cooking up a plan of his own.
Koschei Enslaves One of the Human Queens

In Chapter 33 of “A Court of Wings and Ruin,” Elain, who’s a seer, shares a vision about a “sorcerer-lord” who holds captive one of the human queens who allied with Hybern in the war. She lives as a firebird by day, human by night, and the sorcerer-lord also possesses an “onyx box” that’s more vital to him than anything.
“He keeps other girls — others so like her,” Elain says. “... He keeps them all at the lake.”

In Chapter 54, readers learn more about what happened to this human queen. Her name is Vassa, and, when she refused to join the queens in allying with Hybern, they found a death-lord who enslaves and curses young women and gave her over to him. All this time, the human queens have been claiming she’d fallen ill.

Vassa then shows up in Chapter 72 to fight Hybern in the war and later explains that she was able to come because the Archeron sisters’ father cut a deal with her keeper to release her from the lake temporarily. What exactly that deal is, she does not say.
It’s not until the next book, “A Court of Silver Flames,” that Vassa reveals her keeper is Koschei.
Koschei Wants to Be Free — to Do What?

In “A Court of Silver Flames,” the war against Hybern is won but the Night Court is hearing about bigger threats. In Chapter 7, Vassa, who’s been residing in Prythian’s mortal lands during her time away from the lake, tells her allies that Koschei would do anything to be liberated and may be leveraging a relationship with one of the other human queens, Briallyn.

“I fear what may happen if he ever gets free of the lake,” she tells Cassian. “If he sees this world on the cusp of disaster and knows he could strike, and strike hard, and make himself its master. As he once tried to do, long ago.”

In Chapter 20, Azriel learns more about what they’re up to: Briallyn, who, back in the second book, gleefully jumped into the Cauldron to become immortal but came out a crone, is trying to find her way back to the Cauldron to “retrieve her youth.” Koschei is helping her cause — by pointing her in the direction of the Dread Trove, the magical items connected to the Cauldron — so he too can use the Cauldron to unbind him from the lake.
Briallyn is defeated by Nesta at the end of “A Court of Silver Flames” — but Koschei’s scheming is just beginning.

title: I’m a Therapist Trained to Read Facial Cues. This Is Why ‘You Can See Everything’ Is So Unsettling
summary: A psychologist reacts to You Can See Everything, why it’s such an unsettling experience and the body language of Elizabeth Holmes, Nathan Fielder and Billy Evans.
story: “Take it From Me” is a TODAY series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this edition, a licensed therapist with a degree in cognitive neuroscience weighs in on “You Can See Everything.”
Spoilers ahead for “You Can See Everything.”
If you walk into the “You Can See Everything” expecting answers, you might come out of the theater with more questions.

And if you walk into “You Can See Everything” as a clinical psychologist who studies body language and facial cues, you immediately get another ticket. At least that was the case for Morgan Starr-Riestis, who, as of Oct. 20, saw the documentary following Elizabeth Holmes twice since its Oct. 16 release.
Starr-Riestis, a therapist who has a specific training in nervous system regulation, body language and facial cues, says the movie is an “unsettling” experience.

“We’ve learned to track each other’s facial expressions and micro expressions. To be honest, as somebody that’s trained in this, it was hard to read, especially the first half of it,” she tells TODAY.com.

The documentary, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, opens 34 days before Holmes, convicted in 2022 on four counts of fraud related to her work with her health technology start-up Theranos, surrenders to prison.

Already attracting Oscar buzz (unexpected, considering a documentary has never been up for best picture), critics are calling it “a fascinatingly intimate portrait of a deluded or disingenuous scammer.”

Famous for becoming the world’s youngest female billionaire, Holmes was convicted by a jury in California of four federal charges of wire fraud for misrepresenting to investors what Theranos’ blood-testing Edison machines were actually capable of doing.

Fielder attempts to investigate whether Holmes knowingly defrauded investors — whether she intentionally lied. Holmes dodges the characterization in the doc, attesting she has never told a lie before, not even a white lie. Another telling moment involving a famous comedy sketch might indicate she doesn’t pick up on social cues.

But viewers are divided as to whether Holmes is as naive as she seems. And insiders are not convinced by Holmes’ feigning innocence. John Carreyrou, the former Wall Street Journal reporter who shattered Theranos’ image of a revolutionary blood-testing device through his reporting, is skeptical, as is whistleblower Tyler Shultz. Carreyrou called it a “great film” but said there’s “no chance” Holmes was just “along for the ride” with Theranos. Shultz wrote in a review for Stat News, a health and science publication, that she’s “still lying.”

For psychologists, it’s no surprise the film leaves audiences twisted as to who to trust. Is it Fielder, who turns himself into a character? Is Holmes somehow under the sway of her fiancé, Billy Evans, with whom she shares two kids?

Starr-Riestis caveats that body language isn’t always an accurate read of how someone is feeling. “Some people who have trauma histories or grew up around an angry caregiver, for example, can actually be hyper-sensitive to micro expressions more than someone who didn’t because they learned from a young (age) a certain furrow of a brow might be dangerous,” she says.
Not everyone is good at picking up social cues, too. “There’s also a wide range of reasons why someone might not read facial expressions as well — autism as an example,” she says.
Still, with those caveats in mind, here’s what she found on both watches of “You Can See Everything,” all six hours of it.
The ‘Dissociative Gaze’
Starr-Riestis called Holmes’ wide, unblinking stare during conversations with Fielder an example of the “dissociative gaze.”

“When our eyelids are pulled back like that and we’re unblinking, that’s usually a sign of fear or overwhelm. When you pair it with a smile, the mismatch is naturally unsettling. Our nervous systems just register it as something off,” she says.
A ‘Socially Disorienting’ Conversation Style That ‘Leaves Us on Alert’
The conversation style between Fielder and Holmes is unusual enough for it to be notable. Fielder’s style is “socially disorienting,” she says.

“He lets pauses hang, keeps his delivery flat, and doesn’t smooth over awkward moments the way most instinctively do. Normally, those small social cues tell us how to feel, so without them we’re left to read every interaction raw,” she says.
On Holmes’ end, her “words, tone and expression often don’t seem to match: warm, caring content delivered with a steady, still, intense gaze.”
“When someone’s verbal and nonverbal signals don’t line up, our nervous system registers the mismatch before we can name it, and we go on alert,” she says.
Amanda Seyfried’s ‘Warmth’ Is a Contrast

For Starr-Riestis, the movie changed in the third act when Amanda Seyfried unexpectedly enters the scene. Seyfried portrayed Holmes in the Hulu scripted series “The Dropout.” She reprises the role in “You Can See Everything” and also interacts with Evans, Fielder and Holmes (via a prison phone call) directly.
“What was a refreshing change was having Amanda’s facial cues. She’s so easy to read. You can watch the way her eyebrows rustle when she’s disturbed,” Starr-Riestis says.
Seyfried’s “warmth” is “absent in both Nathan and Elizabeth,” Starr-Riestis says. “To have both him and Elizabeth in the same room, you’re void of a lot of the normal social cues.”
Billy Evans ‘Staring Off’ and ‘Leaving the Room’
Starr-Riestis paid attention to Evans’ movements in the movie.
Evans, who met Holmes before she was indicted, frequently clashed with Fielder in the name of trying to protect Holmes. But some — including Seyfried — say he was controlling.
“You could see him staring off a lot. It felt like he was really trying to keep his anger in,” she says.
She says it seemed like he was trying to “be on his best behavior,” but he “had a hard time hiding it.”
“He would need to leave at certain points or remove himself because it felt like he was just keeping it all bottled (in),” she says.
‘Not Enough Cues’ to Find Out What’s Real
The movie leaves viewers feeling like they don’t know who, or what, to trust.
“I don’t have enough cues to figure out what’s real in this situation,” Starr-Riestis says.
The movie points to an “uncomfortable truth” she says we need to live with: “Each of us are living in our subjective universes.”

“I see it as a Venn diagram. There is overlap in our experience to where we can agree on things and have some sort of shared truth,” she says. “But you can’t see into someone else’s brain and perspective and perception. We can only know a portion of the truth.”

title: ‘10 Things I Hate About You’ Star David Krumholtz Shares Why He Missed the ‘DWTS’ Reunion
summary: David Krumholtz is explaining why he wasn’t able to join his fellow “10 Things I Hate About You” co-stars during their reunion on “Dancing With the Stars.”
story: David Krumholtz is explaining why he wasn’t able to join his fellow “10 Things I Hate About You” co-stars during their reunion on “Dancing With the Stars.”

The actor, who portrayed Michael in the ‘90s rom-com, was missing from the ballroom during the Oct. 20 Dedication Night episode when Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Gabrielle Union, Larisa Oleynik, Andrew Keegan and Susan May Pratt supported Julia Stiles’ emotional tribute to the late Heath Ledger.
Krumholtz shared in an Instagram video Oct. 21 that he would’ve loved to reunite with the cast, but he is currently across the country working on his next project.

“Good morning, here I am in the Catskill Mountains, upstate New York. Fall foliage in full effect,” he said as he panned the camera to show his surroundings. “I am here shooting a film. I could not be in LA for ‘Dancing With the Stars’ last night. I would have loved, loved, loved to have been there.”
He praised the “10 Things I Hate About You” cast before applauding Stiles’ performance.
“Julia’s tribute to my dear friend, who I miss every single day, was amazing and stunning, and I’m so proud of her,” Krumholtz added.
He then reiterated how incredible the cast looked before joking that their appearances played a role in his absence.

“I thought the cast looked amazing. They all look so young still, and it would have been weird because I shaved what’s left of my hair,” he quipped. “Then it becomes a whole internet fodder. ‘Oh, look what happened to him.’ And oh, ‘He’s really…’ I didn’t want that, but that’s not why I wasn’t there. I would have dealt with it.”
At the end of the video he said, “Anyway, love them all. Love you all.”
Stiles confirmed that a scheduling conflict kept Krumholtz away from the ballroom when she spoke to “Entertainment Tonight” after the episode aired.

In a clip posted on Instagram, she revealed that the first person she reached out to about honoring Ledger was Gordon-Levitt. She then contacted Oleynik, whom she has “kept in touch (with) really in a nice way.” Next, Union, Pratt and Keegan agreed to show up.
“But it was like, everyone was kind of like, ‘I’ll do it if everybody else does it.’ So it just took one, you know? And it was so special to have them here,” Stiles shared.

Making sure not to leave out Krumholtz, she continued, “Oh! But wait I have to say, for the record, very important PSA: David Krumholtz, we wanted him here. He wanted to be here, but he’s working on an HBO show in New York, so there was no way he could fly to Los Angeles.”

Stiles and her partner Ezra Sosa performed a contemporary routine for their Dedication Night performance set to “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You” by Frankie Valli, the song Ledger’s character sings to Stiles’ character in “10 Things I Hate About You” to convince her to go on a date with him.
Prior to the dance, Stiles opened up about how much working with Ledger, who died of an accidental overdose in 2008, meant to her. She recalled their moments on set and praised his “lust for life.”

At the end of the performance, the “10 Things I Hate About You” cast embraced one other as a photo of Stiles and Ledger from the film was displayed. Her unforgettable speech to him played through the silent ballroom.
The “DWTS” Instagram account later shared a video of the cast celebrating Stiles’ dance.

title: She Was 6 When She Played Zuzu in ‘It’s a Wonderful Life.’ Now 86, She Weighs in on New Jimmy Stewart Biopic
summary: Karolyn Grimes, once the little girl in It’s a Wonderful Life, had feedback for KJ Apa after seeming him in the new Jimmy Stewart biopic.
story: Karolyn Grimes played the part of 6-year-old Zuzu Bailey alongside Jimmy Stewart’s George Bailey in the 1946 holiday classic “It’s a Wonderful Life,” so she has firsthand knowledge of what the iconic actor was like.
When actor KJ Apa was portraying the legendary Oscar winner in the new movie, “Jimmy,” he got some direct feedback about his performance from Grimes, 86, who makes an appearance in the film.

“It’s interesting because my first time meeting her on set, she looked at me and she goes, ‘Huh. You look nothing like Jimmy Stewart,’” Apa said on TODAY Oct. 21 while laughing. “I was like, ‘Ohhhh.’”
The “Riverdale” star won her over with his portrayal of Stewart’s time as a fighter pilot in World War II as well as a few of his famous acting roles.

“Then I saw her after she watched the movie and she came and she said some really, really kind words,” Apa said. “And to have her stamp of approval meant a lot. Her and (Stewart’s daughter) Kelly, those were the only two people I was like, ‘If they’re happy with it, I can walk away really happy.’”
A sweet moment between Apa and Grimes after she first saw the film was captured in a photo Apa shared on Instagram on Oct. 9.

“I was so moved to feel the love & legacy that Jimmy left behind,” Apa wrote. “His life and work has made such an impact on so many of us and I could feel it last night. I am honored and grateful to have the opportunity to embody a man who loved his country, his family and lead through service. Jimmy Stewart was a good man. A decent man who always strove to do the right thing especially when it wasn’t easy. A simple and powerful reminder for all of us.”

Apa said he worked closely with dialect coach Eliza Simpson to embody Stewart’s inimitable voice and was busy “soaking in every part of him.” Stewart’s daughter Kelly Stewart-Harcourt gave her seal of approval to the film, which hits theaters on Nov. 6.

“But I was thrilled because the problem with somebody playing Dad ... was that you don’t want to sit there and listen to a Jimmy Stewart impersonation for two hours,” Stewart-Harcourt told Entertainment Weekly. “And Dad has such a distinctive way of speaking. It’s hard not to do an impersonation, but KJ channels him and brings him to life without doing a Jimmy Stewart impersonation. So I don’t see how they could have found anybody better.”

“Nothing makes me happier than Jimmy’s daughter Kelly loving the movie,” Apa said on TODAY. “That was the most important thing to me. People who love Jimmy, there’s so many of them. I had no idea it was that extensive how far his movies have reached.”
Apa used Stewart-Harcourt as a resource to learn more about her famous father, who died in 1997 at 89 years old.
“She shared so many stories about her father,” Apa said. “It was really special to have her involved every step of the way so that we could tell an authentic story.”

title: An Emotional ‘DWTS’ Dedication Night Ends With Shocking News
summary: It’s Dedication Night on “Dancing With the Stars,” and the 10 remaining couples are performing emotional and heartfelt routines.
story: It’s Dedication Night on “Dancing With the Stars” and it’s sure to be an emotional one.
The remaining 10 couples are performing routines honoring the special people and places in their lives during the Tuesday, Oct. 20 episode.

After last week’s elimination of fan favorites Guillermo Rodriguez and Witney Carson, the pairs will give it their all to make it another week. In a turn of events, eliminated pro Alan Bersten is filling in for Val Chmerkovskiy after being suspended for his reaction to Carrie Ann Inaba’s critique of his wife Jenna Johnson’s performance.
His absence was quickly mentioned at the top of the episode by co-host Alfonso Ribeiro, who noted, “As you can see Alan Bersten is with Jenna Dewan because Val is not with us this week.”
As the night kicked off, Ribeiro and Julianne Hough welcomed Kym Johnson as she joined Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough as a guest judge.
The first dance by Ezra Frech got the judges emotional. He performed a contemporary dedicated to his mother, who joined him on the ballroom floor.
Tatyana Ali also invited Ribeiro, who portrayed her TV brother on  “The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air,” to join her Viennese waltz in honor of the late James Avery.
Julie Stiles also had a wonderful moment when she reunited the cast of “10 Things I Hate About You” while honoring their late co-star Heath Ledger.

title: ‘10 Things I Hate About You’ Cast Reunites During Julia Stiles’ Heath Ledger ‘DWTS’ Dedication Night Tribute
summary: Julia Stiles gave us 10 things to love about her “Dancing With the Stars” Dedication Night performance.
story: Julia Stiles gave us 10 things to love about her “Dancing With the Stars” Dedication Night performance.

During the Oct. 20 episode, Stiles and partner Ezra Sosa performed a heartfelt contemporary routine set to “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You” by Frankie Valli. The performance was in honor of her late “10 Things I Hate About You” co-star Heath Ledger, who died of an accidental overdose in 2008.
Fans of the film know the song very well, as it’s the one that Ledger’s character Patrick sings to Stiles’ Kat while she’s at soccer practice and he’s trying to make her go on a date with him.
Stiles said during rehearsals that she wishes she could call up Ledger and tell him how much people still love their movie. She said their dance would show his “lust for life.”
The performance was emotional and uplifting. It gave nods to Ledger and the film, before it ended with Stiles putting a flower on the steps.
A photo of Stiles and Ledger was shown on the screen, as her iconic “I Hate You” speech from the film was heard.
Fans got a bigger surprise when the “10 Things I Hate About You” cast appeared on the ballroom floor.
Andrew Keegan, Susan May Pratt, Larisa Oleynik, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Larisa Oleynik and Gabrielle Union surrounded Stiles as the routine ended.
The cast had also created a video before the episode, sharing how they were in attendance to support their girl.
Stiles had previously teased “some special surprises.”

“Making ‘10 Things I Hate About You’ with him was such a special moment in time,” she said in a clip shared days before. “It’s amazing that people still care about that movie, and it’s just sad that we can’t celebrate it with him.”
Sosa also expressed how honored and grateful he was for the opportunity.

“We felt like this routine is so important, not just to honor Heath, but to celebrate the joy and capture his essence in that time that you guys had together filming ‘10 Things I Hate About You,’” he said.
Released in 1999, the teen rom-com is loosely based on William Shakespeare’s “The Taming of the Shrew.” Set in Seattle, Washington, it follows sisters Kat (Stiles) and Bianca Stratford (Oleynik).

Desperate to have a more exciting social life and go to prom, Bianca teams up with new student Cameron (Gordon-Levitt) — who is head-over-heels for her — to find someone to date Kat, an outspoken and independent feminist. Enter Patrick, the bad boy from Australia, who gets paid to woo Kat.
To prepare for the big night, Stiles and Sosa re-created Kat and Patrick’s memorable paintball scene.
They also did the voiceover where Stiles took over Ledger’s lines, while Sosa did hers.
